findings.title: Fast-path exact-length checks for *[]float64/*[]float32 now untested
findings.claim: The fast-path exact-length checks at marshal.go:1012 and marshal.go:1023 are now covered only by accident: existing wrong_data_len tests send too-short payloads that the new bound rejects first, so no test exercises these checks on too-long payloads; if the checks were loosened, extra bytes would be silently accepted.

findings.title: Empty non-NULL payload with dimensions > 0 erroring is an untested behavior change
findings.claim: The PR-declared behavior change where an empty non-NULL payload with dimensions above 0 now errors (marshal.go:998) has no test; every short-payload case uses 2 bytes and every []byte{} case uses dimension 0 (marshal_vector_test.go:641), so reverting the guard from len(data) > 0 to data != nil would silently reintroduce zero-value decoding without any test failing.

findings.title: vectorElemMinSize recomputes isVectorVariableLengthType recursively, causing quadratic…
findings.claim: vectorElemMinSize (marshal.go:1130, marshal.go:1135) calls the recursive isVectorVariableLengthType at every level of its own recursion, making decode cost depth² instead of depth for deeply nested vector types, repeated per inner element; a malicious peer could use this to burn CPU, though it cannot crash the driver.

findings.title: New comment incorrectly claims every path below allocates
findings.claim: The new comment at marshal.go:986 says "every path below turns it into an allocation," but the array path allocates nothing and instead computes element size as len(data)/Dimensions, decoding a short payload as zeros; a reader trusting the comment could wrongly exempt the array path from the new bound.

findings.title: Stale comment about nil/empty and dim=0 falling through to the generic path
findings.claim: The unchanged comment at marshal.go:1006 stating "nil/empty and dim=0 fall through to the generic path" is now stale, since the new bound rejects an empty non-nil payload with dimensions above 0 before reaching that point.

findings.title: Commit message allegedly contradicts the recursive minimum-size logic it introduces
findings.claim: A claim that commit 0276a66's message ("every element takes at least one byte") contradicts the recursive minimum-size logic the same commit adds was raised and judged a false positive by Codex.
